stem: A SaaS company's PostgreSQL database on Amazon RDS shows inconsistent query latency during nightly batch loads, and the database team has confirmed the bottleneck is storage I/O rather than compute. Which TWO changes directly relieve an I/O-bound RDS storage bottleneck? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Move the DB instance to a burstable-performance (db.t) instance class
Provision additional IOPS on the existing General Purpose SSD (gp3) volume
Increase only the DB instance's compute size to a larger memory-optimized class
Migrate the volume to Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) storage
Add a read replica in the same Region to run the nightly batch job's reporting queries

rationale: Provisioning more IOPS on the existing gp3 volume and migrating to io2 storage both act directly on storage I/O capacity, which is the confirmed bottleneck here. A burstable instance class and a larger memory-optimized class both change compute, not storage I/O, and a burstable class can throttle under sustained load besides. A read replica moves read traffic to a separate instance but leaves the primary's own storage I/O bottleneck for its batch load untouched.
